RF Materials.why: Makes hermetic ceramic (HTCC) packages for optical pump-laser modules and TOSA transceiver packages; its optical packages ship to Lumentum's pump modules used in data-center interconnect and optical amplification, so optical-networking build-outs drive its communications-package revenue (44.88% of H1 2026 sales).
RF Materials.evidence: RF Materials half-year report (filed 08-14-2026): optical communications packages are supplied to LUMENTUM, the leader in optical pump modules; two disclosed supply contracts for Lumentum-bound pump laser packages (KRW 7,294,886,200 and KRW 7,553,350,000).

players.product: Hermetic ceramic (HTCC) packages for optical pump-laser modules and TOSA transceivers

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report: H1 2026 consolidated revenue KRW 45,083,321,510 (H1 2025: KRW 28,369,235,445) and operating profit KRW 8,485,958,583 (H1 2025: KRW 2,709,906,879); Q2 2026 revenue KRW 25,059,802,336 (Q2 2025: KRW 16,563,164,568) and Q2 operating profit KRW 5,290,262,133 (Q2 2025: KRW 1,873,048,782); H1 net income KRW 8,615,183,862
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue KRW 45,083,321,510; operating profit KRW 8,485,958,583

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 sales by product: communications packages (hermetic packages for GaN, GaAs and InP compound semiconductors used in RF and optical communications) KRW 20,235M, 44.88% of sales (FY2025: KRW 22,203M, 34.65%); military equipment parts (subsidiary RF Systems) KRW 19,374M, 42.97%; military infrared-sensor packages KRW 2,774M, 6.15%; laser-module packages KRW 383M, 0.85%. Average selling price of communications packages KRW 16,136 in H1 2026 vs KRW 12,039 in FY2025
quarterly_data.figure: communications packages KRW 20,235M (44.88% of H1 2026 sales)

quarterly_data.signal: Customers named in the filing: communications packages are supplied to RFHIC (parent, Korea), MACOM (US) and LUMENTUM (US); RF communications packages go mainly to MACOM and RFHIC, optical communications packages to LUMENTUM, which the company describes as the global leader in optical pump modules, and it aims to enter JDSU, OCLARO and 3S-Photonics. The company says its optical packages are linked to data-center interconnect and optical-amplification products, so demand can rise with data-center infrastructure investment

Customers above 10% of consolidated H1 2026 revenue (names not disclosed): A KRW 9,861,655 thousand (H1 2025: KRW 8,294,973 thousand), B KRW 13,689,380 thousand (H1 2025: KRW 5,326,146 thousand), C KRW 6,471,725 thousand (H1 2025: KRW 4,286,855 thousand); related-party sales to parent RFHIC were KRW 6,471,725 thousand. Overseas revenue KRW 16,803,832 thousand vs KRW 7,547,769 thousand in H1 2025
quarterly_data.figure: Customer B KRW 13,689,380 thousand; overseas revenue KRW 16,803,832 thousand
quarterly_data.counterparty: undisclosed Customers A, B and C; RFHIC

quarterly_data.signal: Optical package development: 400/800G TOSA DML/EML packages for 400/800G transceivers are in the R&D plan; TOSA packages with multilayer HTCC feedthroughs, 10-pin butterfly packages and a localized multilayer package for optical communication modules (for data-center, space and defense uses) are in mass production. H1 2026 R&D expense KRW 2,090,122 thousand (4.64% of revenue)

Capacity: the company says it is preparing to expand production capacity to respond to growing orders and that expanding demand for its products requires facility investment; H1 2026 cash paid for PP&E KRW 3,782,374,123 (H1 2025: KRW 1,020,354,372); contract signed to buy a new headquarters building (KRW 9,753,185 thousand); inventories KRW 24,939,732,251 vs KRW 14,865,993,812 at end-2025

connects_to.relationship: Hermetic packages for optical pump-laser modules
